name: Software AG Adabas
tagline: Inverted-list, multi-value mainframe database paired with Natural, run as a standalone Software AG business.
description: Adabas (Adaptable Database System) is Software AG's high-throughput database from 1971, storing compressed records with multiple-value and periodic-group fields and indexing them through inverted lists of 'descriptors'. Together with the Natural 4GL it runs government, tax, social-security and banking systems on IBM Z, with a Linux edition for distributed and cloud deployments. After Silver Lake took Software AG private and sold off webMethods, StreamSets and others, Adabas & Natural has operated as a standalone business since January 2025 under an 'Adabas & Natural 2050+' commitment; the October 2025 release brought Adabas for z/OS 8.6.1 and Adabas for Linux 7.4. It is a keep-running platform, not a new-build choice.
developer: Software AG (Adabas & Natural business, owned by Silver Lake)

pricing.notes: Enterprise licensing, usually bundled with Natural; mainframe pricing tied to capacity.

scale.notes: Adabas Cluster Services (Parallel Sysplex) and Adabas Cluster for Linux; Event Replicator for downstream copies.

strengths: Very high transaction throughput for large record-oriented workloads
Multiple-value and periodic-group fields avoid many joins
Automatic record compression keeps storage small
Event Replicator streams changes to relational targets and Kafka-style consumers
weaknesses: Natural and Adabas skills are rare and ageing
Proprietary access model; SQL access needs gateways
Ownership has changed repeatedly, adding long-term uncertainty
useCases: Banking and insurance back ends on IBM Z
notIdealFor: Analytics without replication to a warehouse
